question: An object is placed in front of a convex mirror of focal length 9 cm, at a distance of 18 cm. Its image is formed at a distance of:
solution:
The correct answer is** 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Image formation in convex mirror when the Object is Placed Between Infinity and Pole**

 
 
• **​**We take into consideration two distinct rays emanating from the object in this instance of the formation of an image by a convex mirror.
 
• One runs **parallel to the principal axis**, and the other points in the direction of the mirror's **center of curvature**.
 
• After being reflected, the image between the **pole (P) and the focus (F) **behind the mirror is created by these rays.
 
• As a result, a **diminished, virtual, and erect image** is created.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28258f9e4ed252b00360ba2bb8ee5931a10f20f07c2ba409162250ebe2233fb8.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calculations**

 
 
• Given a **convex mirror **

 focal length,** f=9cm**

 object distance, **u=-18cm**

 We know, mirror formula

 **1/v+ 1/u= 1/f**

 1/v+ 1/ (-18) = 1/9

 1/v= 1/9+1/18

 1/v= 2+1/18= 3/18

 1/v= 1/6

 **v= 6cm **
